diagnosis.bottleneck: The query performs a completely unnecessary LEFT JOIN to the promotion table - the join preserves all store_sales rows (since it's LEFT) and no promotion columns are referenced in SELECT or WHERE, so the join cannot change the COUNT(1) result. Time is spent scanning promotion (300 rows), broadcasting it, and executing the join.

plan_nodes.note: LeftOuter BuildRight; Left keys [1]: [ss_item_sk#47975]; Right keys [1]: [p_item_sk#48000]; Join type: LeftOuter; Join c

hypotheses.claim: A LEFT JOIN whose columns are never read still costs a join; if the joined key is unique it cannot change the rows and can be removed. (matched: left join tpcds_db.promotion p on ss.ss_item_sk = p.p_item_sk)

The BroadcastHashJoin LeftOuter is semantically redundant: removing it (and the promotion scan/broadcast) would produce identical results while eliminating the join, broadcast, and promotion I/O entirely.
Scanning the promotion table (node 4) with pushed IsNotNull filter is wasted I/O because the join result is never used; the scan could be removed if the optimizer recognized the unused outer join.
The BroadcastExchange (node 6) serializes and broadcasts the promotion relation to all executors, consuming network and memory for a relation that does not affect the final count.
